blocks.text: Namespaces control what a process can see; cgroups control how much it can use. Docker orchestrates both, plus capabilities, seccomp and AppArmor/SELinux.

rows: App is PID 1, can't see host processes
Own eth0 and loopback; two containers can both bind :8000
Root inside can map to an unprivileged host UID
Container sees its cgroup as root

blocks.text: cgroups: what happens at the limit

items: Memory over limit: kernel OOM killer kills a process, usually exit 137.
CPU over quota: throttled (slower), never killed.
pids limit: fork fails with EAGAIN.

blocks.text: Namespaces can be shared on purpose: `--network container:web` joins another container's net namespace. Kubernetes pods share one net namespace, which is why pod containers talk on localhost.

Runtimes often read host values: `os.cpu_count()` returns 64 inside a `--cpus=2` container, and `free` shows host RAM. Auto-sized worker pools then over-spawn and hit OOM. Set WEB_CONCURRENCY, OMP_NUM_THREADS explicitly.

Q: "What happens when a container exceeds its CPU vs memory limit?" A: "CPU is throttled by the CFS quota and just runs slower; memory triggers the cgroup OOM killer, which SIGKILLs a process (exit 137, OOMKilled=true)."

items: Memory limit kills, CPU limit throttles.
Shared net namespace explains pod-local localhost.
Don't trust host-wide values like os.cpu_count() inside containers.
